explanation: Move one pointer by one link and another by two. They meet exactly when a reachable cycle exists.
correctness: Without a cycle the faster pointer reaches null. Within a cycle its relative position advances by one per iteration and eventually equals the slower pointer.
walkthrough: For values [2,2,9] with tail link -1, the last node points to null. The repeated payload 2 does not imply a cycle: the two nodes are different objects. The fast pointer reaches the end, so return false. JSON supplies [listValues,tailLinkIndex]; -1 means a null tail. The callable receives only the constructed entry node and returns a boolean based on node identity.
edgeCases: An empty entry returns false. A node pointing to itself returns true; distinct nodes with equal values do not constitute a cycle.
timeComplexity: O(n) time: an acyclic fast pointer reaches null after at most n links; after entering a cycle, the relative offset advances by one and meets within at most n more steps.
spaceComplexity: O(1) auxiliary space: two node references, with no visited set.
